title: He broke the bread…
paragraphs:
He broke the bread…
and exposed the hunger no one wanted to admit.

You smiled.
You posted.
You showed up strong.
And you don’t even know how to say it.

You’ve been feeding your image…
but neglecting your soul.

You’ve been consuming everything—
attention, validation, pleasure, success—

Still restless.
Still searching.
Still hungry.
Let me say what most won’t.

You can look alive on the outside…
and be slowly dying within.

A hidden habit.
A secret compromise.
A private addiction no one sees.

“Just one more time.”
“I’ll stop tomorrow.”
“No one will know.”

Scroll more.
Work harder.
Chase another relationship.
Numb it with entertainment.
Because you are trying to feed a spiritual hunger with temporary things.
This is the tension the crowd felt in John 6.

Bread in their hands.
Bellies full.
“Truly, truly, I say to you, you are seeking me, not because you saw signs, but because you ate your fill of the loaves.” — John 6:26

“You don’t want Me.
You want what I can give you.”
Then Jesus drops the line that shattered their expectations:
“I am the bread of life; whoever comes to me shall not hunger, and whoever believes in me shall never thirst.” — John 6:35
You don’t just need what Jesus provides.
And this is where it gets uncomfortable.
Because Jesus didn’t come to decorate your life.
He came to replace what’s killing you.
It feels good for a moment.

Then comes the guilt.
The shame.
The distance from God.
“For the wages of sin is death…” — Romans 6:23
Emptiness that nothing in this world can fill.
“…but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.” — Romans 6:23
You see, Jesus didn’t just identify your hunger.
By becoming the Bread that would be broken.

Your hidden shame.
Your private failures.
Your secret compromises.
“He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree…” — 1 Peter 2:24
“Eat my flesh and drink my blood” (John 6:53),
He was calling for total dependence.
A complete receiving of Him by faith.

(Some scholars interpret this as symbolic language pointing to belief in His sacrifice, while others see deeper sacramental meaning—but both point to this: you must receive Christ, not just admire Him.)
This is where many walked away.
And maybe that’s where you are.
Jesus is not an add-on to your life.
“I have come that they may have life and have it abundantly.” — John 10:10
But it only comes one way.
“I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.” — John 14:6
So what does it mean to receive the Bread of Life?
You stop feeding on things that are destroying you.
And trusting that Jesus is enough.
You are not too far gone.
so you could be made whole.
So now the question is not:
“Whoever comes to me I will never cast out.” — John 6:37

With your mess.
With your questions.
With your struggle.
